ask:
Kill guard knows a lane's left-behind server (c27), claude-settings, on this Mac. Goal: a session can stop, by pid, a test server that one of its own lane agents started, after that agent ended. A process this session did not start stays refused. No new per-call cost.

Today (main 149f4bc5): hooks/guard_kill.py foreign_pid_kill(tokens, transcript) allows a kill by pid only when the parent chain reaches this session's claude process. When an agent ends, macOS hands its server to init (PPID 1), so the guard calls it foreign. The one exception, in_own_agent_worktree, needs the cwd inside .claude/worktrees/agent-<id> AND <session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl. Lane agents work in scratchpad folders, and workflow agents keep records under subagents/workflows/, so it never matches them. Decision a-kill-by-pid-needs-an-owned-pid lists this as a known limit.

1. First check, before any code. Start `sleep 600 &` from a Bash call inside a subagent, let the subagent end, and confirm: (a) the sleep's PPID is 1; (b) its environment holds CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID equal to the hook payload's session_id, read the way step 2 will; (c) where the subagent's record landed under subagents/. If (b) fails, stop and report. Do not fall back to path rules.

2. Ownership by inherited tag. In guard_kill.py, beside in_own_agent_worktree: a pid is owned when its PPID is 1 and its environment holds CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID exactly equal to this session's id. guard.py already reads the id with session_id_of(payload); pass it into foreign_pid_kill. Read the environment with no child process: Mac sysctl KERN_PROCARGS2 through ctypes (argv and env come back separately, so a match in argv does not count); Linux /proc/<pid>/environ. Match a whole NAME=value entry, never a substring. Any read failure means foreign. Read it only on the path that already found the pid foreign, so an allowed kill costs nothing new. Keep the worktree exception. Windows stays as today.

3. Reap at session end, not agent end (advisor, Oct 26, after the Mac first check). The session and all its agents share one scratchpad, a server started with `cmd & echo $!` gets PPID 1 as soon as its Bash call ends, and the env tag holds only the session id, so an agent-end reap would stop live servers of the main session and of sibling lanes. So janitor/agent_end_reap.py stays as it is (it reaps only by an agent's own worktree). Add the tag test to janitor/session_end_sweep.py instead: at SessionEnd, stop each process whose PPID is 1, whose env holds CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID exactly equal to the ending session's id, and whose cwd sits in that session's scratchpad. The whole session is ending, so nothing it owns is still in use. Any read failure means keep. The script still always exits 0 and stays inside its timeout. Do not tag servers per agent at launch: no agent id exists in the env, and adding one means rewriting every Bash call, a per-call cost. One shared helper for the tag read, imported by guard_kill.py and session_end_sweep.py. Tests: the SessionEnd reap stops a tagged scratchpad orphan, and keeps one with another session's id, one with no tag, and one outside the scratchpad. Update decision agent-end-reap-stops-what-a-finished-agent-left in place to say scratchpad orphans are reaped at session end, and why.

4. One brief line. Where lane briefs are written (find the home; add no second one): a lane stops each server it started before it ends, by $! from the same call or through the harness.

Tests, red on main and green on the fix: a PPID-1 process carrying this session's id is allowed; the same with another session's id is denied; one with no tag is denied; one whose argv, not env, holds the id is denied; pids 0, 1 and -1 stay denied. Add a mutant in hooks/mutate_guard.py that drops the exact-match check, and show a test kills it. Update decision a-kill-by-pid-needs-an-owned-pid in place: one dated owner line (Oct 21, ownership by inherited session tag) and fix its Limits list.

Ship as one PR under the repo's normal review and merge rules. Report: the first-check results, diff size per file, test names, the two decisions' before and after text, and the PR.
note: Checked at 149f4bc5. hooks/guard_kill.py lets a session kill a pid only when its parent chain reaches the session; a lane agent's server re-parented to pid 1 is foreign, and the one exception (cwd in .claude/worktrees/agent-<id> plus a matching subagents/ record) misses scratchpad lanes and workflow agents. The agent-end reaper has the same blind spot. Your ruling, Oct 21: ownership = parent is 1 and the process environment holds this session's CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID (from guard.py's session_id_of), read only when a kill would otherwise be refused; plus one brief line telling lanes to stop their own servers. Unmeasured: that the tag is present on the Mac; the brief's first check measures it and stops if not. Mac only. Brief rewritten Oct 26 as one paste block (project files briefs-live/c27-mac-kill-guard.md) and handed to you; not yet run. Mac first check, Oct 26: the tag is present (orphan env holds CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and CLAUDE_PID, no agent id); the agent-end payload carries session_id and scratchpad_dir. Finding: agents share the session's scratchpad and a backgrounded server is PPID 1 while still in use, so an agent-end reap would stop live servers. Advisor pick, Oct 26: the kill guard lane stands as briefed; scratchpad orphans are reaped at SessionEnd in session_end_sweep.py, not at agent end; no per-agent tag (no agent id in env; adding one costs every Bash call). Brief step 3 rewritten; owner to pass it on.
title: Let a session stop the test servers its lane agents left
why: Your report, Oct 21: on Mac, a lane agent's test server is handed to the system (parent pid 1) when the agent ends. The kill guard then calls it foreign and refuses the kill, so the server keeps running and holds its port and memory.
